patch.objective: Identity and access monitoring: detecting credential misuse and privilege escalation

sources.cite: CompTIA CySA+ CS0-004 Exam Objectives, Exam Objectives Document Version 2.0 (exam launched 2026-06-23; domains 34/26/24/16)
sources.note: Relevant text: 1.2 'Given a scenario, analyze indicators of potential malicious activity' (host-related indicators: resource consumption, unauthorized software, anomalous activity: suspicious or rogue processes, Living Off the Land Binaries (LOLBins) and Scripts, file system changes, data exfiltration); 2.3 'Given a scenario, analyze data to prioritize and mitigate vulnerabilities' (exploitability, active exploitation/threat intelligence, asset value, impact, patch/remediation availability, true/false positives, true/false negatives; CVSS metrics, EPSS); 3.2 'Summarize the incident response process' (containment, recovery); 3.3 'Given a scenario, implement incident response techniques' (triage, establishment of a timeline, determining severity and impact, escalation; isolating affected targets, remediation and verification, release from isolation, performing restoration). Read in the official objectives PDF (the course's officialObjectivesUrl) through a summarizing fetch, and the CompTIA V4 page, on 2026-11-11. CS0-003 retires for English on 2026-12-22. Reused for REQ-336 from this course's alert-triage-lolbin-hunt (the same reading and date); the objective wording is the course seed's.

sources.cite: CompTIA Security+ V8 (SY0-801): launch on or around 2026-11-17; up to 90 questions, 90 minutes, pass 750 (100-900); domains 16/24/19/27/14; Security Operations includes 'Implement incident response activities' (preparation, detection, containment, recovery, lessons learned)
sources.note: Read through a summarizing fetch on 2026-11-11. The SY0-801 objectives document (Version 2.0) is the course's official source and was not re-read here.

sources.cite: NIST SP 800-61 Rev. 3, Incident Response Recommendations and Considerations for Cybersecurity Risk Management
sources.note: Relevant text: A CSF 2.0 Community Profile (April 2025; supersedes Rev. 2): RS.MI-01 'Incidents are contained'; RS.MI-02 'Incidents are eradicated'; RS.AN-03 analysis and root cause; RS.AN-07 'Incident data and metadata are collected, and their integrity and provenance are preserved'; RS.CO-02 'Internal and external stakeholders are notified of incidents'; RC.RP-03 'The integrity of backups and other restoration assets is verified before using them for restoration'. The current revision. Subcategory wording read in the PDF (nvlpubs.nist.gov) through a summarizing fetch on 2026-11-11; the publication date and the supersession read on the CSRC news page. Rev. 3 replaces the Rev. 2 four-phase life cycle with the CSF 2.0 Functions; Security+ still names the older phases.

sources.cite: CISA, Federal Government Cybersecurity Incident and Vulnerability Response Playbooks (November 2021)
sources.note: Relevant text: containment includes 'Isolating impacted systems and network segments', 'Capturing forensic images to preserve evidence for legal use (if applicable) and further investigation', 'Blocking (and logging) of unauthorized accesses; blocking malware sources', 'Changing system admin passwords, rotating private keys, and service/application account secrets where compromise is suspected'; 'Before moving to eradication, ensure that all means of persistent access into the network have been accounted for'. Read through a summarizing fetch on 2026-11-11. Written for federal agencies; the containment, evidence and persistence steps are general practice.

sources.cite: Microsoft Learn, 'Responding to a compromised email account' (updated 2026-07-17)
sources.note: Relevant text: symptoms include inbox rules that forward mail to unknown addresses and recently added external forwarding; 'Disabling the compromised account is preferred and highly recommended until you complete the investigation'; 'If you can't disable the account, the next best step is to reset the password'; 'Revoking active sessions immediately invalidates any active access using the stolen credentials'; review and remove unrecognized MFA methods, consented apps, admin roles, mail forwarders and inbox rules; review the audit logs from the onset of the suspicious activity. Vendor guidance for one mail platform, used for the account steps; the scenario names no product. Read through a summarizing fetch on 2026-11-11.

sources.cite: CrowdStrike, 2026 Global Threat Report (press release, 2026-02-24): 'The average eCrime breakout time fell to just 29 minutes in 2025', the fastest observed 27 seconds; breakout time is the time an adversary takes to move from the first compromised host to another (2025 report)
sources.note: Vendor telemetry, not a standard. Used only to set the scale of the attacker's clock (tens of minutes, not hours); the scenario's own step times are the author's.
